items.headline: Super for housing
items.note: Replaces the mismatched Payday Super administrative item. Andrew Bragg’s official 22 September 2026 speech argues for super to support home ownership and challenges Labor, while explicitly saying the ideas are not Coalition policy. The label presents the housing-policy debate, not an enacted right to withdraw compulsory super, financial advice, or a settled Coalition proposal. Labor’s broader defence of super is recorded in the Treasurer’s official 19 August 2026 press conference; no more specific current Labor position is inferred here.

items.headline: Child safety
items.note: Safety obligations and risks from generative AI, including harms to children. eSafety position statement provides issue depth; distinct from childcare affordability and the original domestic-safety topic.

items.headline: Mental health
items.note: Access to care, trauma and administrative barriers for veterans and first responders. Existing P4A issue discussion, with clinical-path follow-through; not individual medical advice or a claim that AI causes a particular condition.

items.headline: Gas prices
items.note: Domestic affordability, export incentives and bargaining power. ACCC gas inquiry provides dated market reports and the LNG netback series. An LNG netback benchmark is not an overseas household bill: comparisons need the same period, market, units, contract basis and treatment of shipping, liquefaction, transport and retail costs. No assertion that overseas consumers always pay less.

items.headline: Corporate tax
items.note: Who contributes and who benefits from resources and data centres. The official 1 October 2026 interview addresses public concerns and the government’s response. Company income tax applies to taxable profits, not gross revenue; nil income tax alone does not establish avoidance. Resource royalties, company income tax and petroleum resource rent tax (PRRT) are different measures and must not be conflated. No blanket claim that gas companies pay no tax.

items.headline: Multinational tax avoidance
items.note: International profit shifting and gaps between tax systems, and collective policy responses. OECD BEPS explains the mechanisms and reform agenda. Distinct from the domestic corporate-tax contribution topic; no unverified allegation about a named company or person.

items.headline: Resource profits
items.note: Who receives the value from extraction of publicly owned resources, and how licences, royalties and public-benefit terms should work. Distinct from gas consumer prices, corporate income tax and offshore avoidance. Petroleum ownership is held by Australian governments on behalf of the community; mineral ownership and extraction rights require the relevant jurisdiction and tenure to be identified. Resource ownership and a mining/petroleum licence are not the same thing as surface Crown-land leasehold. Do not assume every extraction project occupies leased Crown land or that all citizens endorse one distribution model. The linked P4A room proposes transparent contracts and public-return tests.

preservation.policy: Keep all original topics in their original wording and order. Append new reviewed items; do not replace or delete originals. Original spans had no links or factual claims; local topic links were added on 2026-10-03. Ticker labels must be one to three words; keep explanation and source context in notes and destinations.
